characteristics.Definition: A financial account representing the billing relationship between a customer and the provider, tracking charges, payments, and outstanding balances.
A natural or legal person who purchases or subscribes to products and services from a telecommunications provider. The Customer entity is the central anchor for the Customer 360 domain.
Any touchpoint or engagement between a customer and the provider across physical or digital channels, including calls, chats, store visits, and app sessions.
A formal request by a customer to purchase, modify, or cancel a product or service offering, tracked through fulfillment lifecycle stages.
An ongoing contractual agreement entitling a customer to consume a specific service for a defined period, with associated pricing and SLA terms.

transformation.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_customers FROM dp.curated.customer_360 WHERE status = 'active'

characteristics.Description: Ratio of billing accounts with zero or negative balance (fully collected) to total accounts.

transformation.sql: SELECT SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(balance <= 0), COUNT(*)) AS collection_rate FROM dp.curated.billing_account

characteristics.Description: Ratio of customers churned in the last 30 days to total customers.

transformation.sql: SELECT SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(status = 'churned' AND updated_at >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)), COUNT(*)) AS churn_rate FROM dp.curated.customer_360

characteristics.Description: Ratio of orders in pending or processing status to total orders.

transformation.sql: SELECT SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(status IN ('pending','processing')), COUNT(*)) AS open_orders_rate FROM dp.curated.product_order

characteristics.Description: Month-over-month growth rate of active service subscriptions.

transformation.sql: WITH curr AS (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM dp.curated.service_subscription WHERE status = 'active'), prev AS (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM dp.curated.service_subscription WHERE status = 'active' AND created_at < DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)) SELECT SAFE_DIVIDE(curr.c - prev.c, prev.c) AS growth_rate FROM curr, prev
